titre: GTA 6 Players Have Already Discovered an Infinite Money Glitch
chapo: Grand Theft Auto 6 players have found several ways to make money quick, but not everyone is partaking.
extrait: Many players have a habit of optimizing the fun out of video games, and that tendency has unsurprisingly found its way into Grand Theft Auto 6. Apparently, the game has many ways to “get rich quick,” and these exploitive strategies are going viral online. In one method, the player drives to the Apollo Aggregates warehouse in South Vice-Dale County, where a drug deal went wrong. The building is full of narcotics, spare bills, and dead bodies, letting you easily pillage close to $8,000 worth of loot. After grabbing the goods, the player stores the contraband in their car, then saves and loads to teleport back to their house. At this point, they bring the contraband to Brian’s place to cash out. A YouTube video outlining the method claims you can make around $4,000 every five minutes, which is more efficient than nearly everything else in the early game. In another strategy that falls more into the "glitch" category, the player robs the stores near Jason’s house, loses the cops, and then enters any story mission. After the story mission cutscene begins, the player selects Restart Mission in the menu and then pauses and quits. This causes all the stores the player just robbed to instantly reopen with new loot, allowing them to rob them again. However, despite how efficient these early-game earning strategies are, many players are swearing off the temptation. “Nah I’m good! Didn’t wait 13 years just to glitch my way through the game,” one user wrote on X. “Top tip, if you just play the game the amount of money you can make is unlimited, no special trick needed,” a sardonic YouTube comment reads. These users point out that earning so much money early undermines the game’s economy, ruins the gradual progression of unlocking better gear, and invalidates many of the game’s cash-earning side missions. On top of this, these methods directly counter the narrative flow of GTA 6, which is about Lucia and Jason attempting to scrape together some semblance of the fabled “American Dream.” While some are baffled by why anyone would use such mind-numbing strategies, players are obviously entitled to play the game however they want. Still, it seems likely that Rockstar will patch the game soon to remove these methods, especially the second one, which seems to be a bug. Grand Theft Auto 6 is now available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X.

titre: GTA 6 Players Are Refusing to Make Use of an Infinite Money Glitch They Say Ruins the Experience
chapo: Some GTA 6 players are refusing to make use of an infinite money glitch they say ruins the experience Rockstar set out to provide.
extrait: Players have already found ways to farm infinite money, undermining the carefully paced economy of GTA 6 using multiple methods. While this happens with every game, it’s particularly strange here. Why is it weird? GTA 6 already has infinite money. You can rob as many stores and businesses as you like and fence the goods, and while stores close down for a while after they’ve been robbed, they reset on a frequent basis. You just have to play as intended, but some players are hellbent on farming cash in the most mind-numbing ways possible. The methods are all built around forcing the store closure timers to reset, so you can rob the same stores on repeat. First, they rob a bunch of stores and collect as much as possible, then they trigger a mission to start a cutscene. Once the cutscene begins, they restart the mission from the menu. When the cutscene begins again, they quit out of the mission, which forces all the stores to reset. Honestly, it sounds arduous and you’d be better off exploring to find new robbery opportunities so you can experience fresh gameplay. Another method sees players go to a lucrative building, get all of the money and narcotics from inside, and store them in the trunk of their car. Next they save the game and immediately load it up. The bags remain in your car, but the building’s loot resets, allowing you to rinse and repeat. Most players agree that this is probably the worst way to experience GTA 6. “Nah I’m good! Didn’t wait 13 years just to glitch my way through the game,” said one fan. “Takes away from the experience,” another poster agreed. “The games (sic) way too immersive to just skip the grind, takes the fun out of it.” Another said: “Nah I prefer to just, ya know, play the game and earn it.” There are seemingly dozens of variations of this glitch, with the method slightly varying between them. In another, the player robs a different location and fences the goods before saving and reloading to reset the location’s loot. Again, this genuinely seems like a miserable way to play the game — especially since more exciting and lucrative robbery opportunities open up as you progress through the story. It’s also probably just a matter of time until Rockstar patches it out. Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? Check out the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN.
